sentiment.rationale: The document reports a massive GAAP loss per share of ($14.65) for Q4 2020 and ($20.88) for the full year, with operating cash flow of ($18.4) billion. Forward guidance is effectively lowered: the 777X first delivery is pushed to late 2023 with a $6.5 billion charge, and the 737 MAX production rate remains low with gradual increases only in early 2022. Management's tone is cautious, acknowledging 'continued challenges for commercial aerospace into 2021' and the need to 'preserve liquidity.' These factors indicate a significant negative shift in forward expectations.

summary.revenue: Q4 2020 revenue of $15.3 billion, down 15% from $17.9 billion in Q4 2019. Full-year 2020 revenue of $58.2 billion, down 24% from $76.6 billion in 2019.
summary.eps: Q4 2020 GAAP loss per share of ($14.65), compared to ($1.79) in Q4 2019. Full-year 2020 GAAP loss per share of ($20.88), compared to ($1.12) in 2019.
summary.guidance: 777X first delivery expected in late 2023 (pushed from earlier expectations). 737 program expects to gradually increase production to 31 per month in early 2022. 787 program plans to transition production rate to 5 per month in March 2021. The company will continue business transformation actions in 2021 to preserve liquidity.
summary.margin: Q4 2020 GAAP operating margin of (52.6)%, compared to (12.3)% in Q4 2019. Full-year 2020 GAAP operating margin of (22.0)%, compared to (2.6)% in 2019.
key_risks: COVID-19 pandemic significantly constraining commercial air travel and impacting results
737 MAX grounding and regulatory approval process
777X program $6.5 billion pre-tax charge and delayed first delivery to late 2023
Lower commercial deliveries and services volume due to COVID-19

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: CEO Dave Calhoun stated: 'While the impact of COVID-19 presents continued challenges for commercial aerospace into 2021, we remain confident in our future, squarely-focused on safety, quality and transparency as we rebuild trust and transform our business.' This language acknowledges ongoing challenges while expressing measured confidence.
